content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert 5053214321 — Elevated 5xx and latency observed in us-east-1. Affected: Hosted API + Dedicated GPU pools (us-east-1). Source signals: AWS NAT/egress errors and third-party observability ingestion throttles. Auto-escalating to on-call.
sam_sre: saw it, confirming. Hosted API 5xx rate ~8% at 13:12 UTC, Dedicated pool error budget crossing. Link: https://console.redwood/mon/alerts/5053214321
sam_sre: quick triage: CloudMetrics (observability vendor) shows ingestion backpressure in us-east-1 starting 13:03. AWS NAT gateway error spikes at 13:08. Both correlate with token fetch timeouts.
mia_platform: tagging @leo_oncall — can you take lead? I'm going to check routing/edge fallbacks.
leo_oncall: on it. paging rotation updated, taking ownership. grabbing runbook.
leo_oncall: runbook step1: confirm scope -> checking Dedicated pools
dave_prodeng: Dedicated pools in us-east-1 show increased backend 502 from model-serving proxies. Logs show upstream connection resets to sts/iam endpoints and CloudMetrics timeouts. Short snippet:
```
2026-03-17T13:10:45Z model-proxy ERROR upstream reset: dial tcp: i/o timeout
2026-03-17T13:10:46Z kv-cache WARN observability push failed: 503 service unavailable
```
caroline_support: CS: customers reporting timeouts and token errors. Top customers A and B saw elevated errors starting ~13:15. Ticket queue rising.
anna_cs: drafting customer blurb: "We are investigating an external provider outage affecting API requests in us-east-1. We are routing traffic to alternate regions and working on mitigation. Updates in the incidents channel." Will post once we have ETA.
mia_platform: immediate mitigations: 1) enable cross-region routing to prefer us-west-2 for new requests, 2) trigger Dedicated pool spillover to reserved capacity in us-west-2, 3) enable model-fallback to quantized variant for latency-sensitive endpoints.
sam_sre: applying routing policy tweak now: `redwood-router promote --from-region us-east-1 --to-region us-west-2 --weight 0.6` (dry-run -> live)
sam_sre: executed — traffic shift started at 13:22 UTC. Monitoring latency and error rate.
leo_oncall: also enabling degraded mode for chat endpoints: smaller-quantized models rolled for canary routes. Command:
```
redwood-deploy set --model fallback-gptq-8bit --route /v1/chat --canary 10%
```
leo_oncall: canary looks clean so far, increasing to 40%.
dave_prodeng: opened AWS support case for NAT/egress flaps and pinged CloudMetrics support. Case IDs logged in incident doc.
caroline_support: CS posting initial notice to impacted customers now. :white_check_mark:
anna_cs: posted message. copying into support thread.
sam_sre: 13:30 UTC: 5xx rate reduced to 2.1%, p50/p95 latency improving. Dedicated pool errors dropping. Observability ingestion still lagging (~60s ingest delay) — dashboards delayed.
mia_platform: next steps: continue traffic shift until us-east stabilizes, keep canary for fallback models, keep AWS/CloudMetrics tickets open. If error rate <1% for 15m, start rollback.
leo_oncall: handing off to @mia_platform at 13:40 for monitoring and postmortem. `next-oncall: @mia_platform`
incident-bot: Incident 5053214321 status -> mitigation in progress (routing changed, model fallbacks enabled). Severity: elevated -> monitoring. Pager duty: acknowledged by leo_oncall.
sam_sre: tagging doc -> https://wiki.redwood/incidents/5053214321
caroline_support: support queue stabilized, customers acknowledged the notice.
anna_cs: prepping customer follow-up for 14:00 UTC with update + root-cause pending.
leo_oncall: final note before handoff: no data plane data loss noted, mainly control-plane/egress timeouts to third-party and AWS egress causing 502/503. Good work team. :thumbsup:
mia_platform: taking over, will keep channel updated, scheduling postmortem with AWS/CloudMetrics. Closing active paging after stabilization.
